title: God of Our Mercy and Our Praise
description: God of Our Mercy and Our Praise in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 386 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christ's Love to Enemies our Example”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of our mer-cy and our praise, Thy glo-ry is our song; We'll speak the hon-ors of thy grace With a re-joic-ing tongue.

lines: God of our mercy and our praise,
Thy glory is our song;
We'll speak the honors of thy grace
With a rejoicing tongue.
When Christ among the sons of men
In humble form was found,
With cruel slanders, false and vain,
They compassed him around.
Their miseries his compassion moved,
Their peace he still pursued;
They rendered hatred for his love,
And evil for his good.
Their malice raged without a cause;
Yet, with his dying breath,
He prayed for murderers on his cross,
And blest his foes in death.
O, may his conduct, all divine,
To us a model prove:
Like his, O God, our hearts incline
Our enemies to love.

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
